summary: iteration_7 verified. Backend: 74/74 pytest PASS in 22.4s (60 prior + 14 new tests for register / preferences / score-history / digest). Frontend: 9/10 UI checks PASS. Scheduler startup log 'scheduler started: weekly_digest (mon 15:00 UTC), nightly_rescan (03:00 UTC)' confirmed in backend supervisor logs at import time.

integration_issues.issue: When an already-signed-in user visits /register and submits a duplicate email, Register.useEffect races the 409 handler: because refreshed auth resolves to a valid user, the page navigates to /dashboard before the setErrors({email: ...}) re-render lands — so register-email-error is not observable. Purely a UI race for the specific 'signed-in-then-revisit' path; a signed-out user submitting a duplicate email correctly sees the inline error (verified in backend, endpoint returns 409 'An account with that email already exists'). Suggested fix: on Register mount, if user is signed in, hard-redirect BEFORE render (or short-circuit the submit handler) so the form is never mounted for authed users.

action_items: Optional polish: on /register mount, if user is already authenticated, redirect immediately (before form render) so duplicate-email flow is only reached signed-out. Backend + primary signed-out UX are correct.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1736 lines — approaching the 700-line 'split into modules' guideline. Suggest breaking into auth.py / projects.py / billing.py / digest.py / scheduler.py routers.

APScheduler runs IN-PROCESS on FastAPI (AsyncIOScheduler). This is fine for single-worker uvicorn, but if the app is ever scaled to N workers each will fire the same cron independently — leading to N weekly emails per user. Add a dispatcher lock (e.g., mongo advisory doc with unique index on {job_id, run_key}) before scaling horizontally.
_build_digest_for_user does N+1 mongo queries (one score fetch per project). At scale (>50 projects/user) this will get slow. Consider a $group aggregation on scores collection.
digest_preview endpoint returns the FULL rendered HTML (~2KB+) for every preview call — fine for on-demand /preview but note it isn't paginated. Acceptable given the endpoint is user-initiated.

_send_email wraps resend.Emails.send with asyncio.to_thread but does not enforce a timeout — a slow Resend response will hold the FastAPI worker. Consider asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=15) to fail fast to 502 (currently observed correctly on non-owner recipients).

score_history sort=-1 + docs.reverse() works but returns only the newest N points chronologically — for a very active project (>100 scans) the chart would silently drop old history. Acceptable given limit clamps to 100.

Digest send-test in Resend TEST mode returns 502 (not 500) for non-key-owner recipients — test accepts 200 OR 502, tolerates non-JSON 502 body (some upstream 502s come back as HTML from the ingress).
rca of the issue: Register duplicate-email UI edge case is a mount-time race between useAuth() resolving a signed-in user (→ navigate('/dashboard')) and the /auth/register 409 handler (→ setErrors). Reproduction: (1) POST /api/auth/register email A → cookie set, useAuth.user populates; (2) client-side navigate to /register — form briefly mounts; (3) submit same email A → 409; (4) simultaneously the useEffect fires navigate('/dashboard', {replace:true}) because user is truthy, unmounting the error before it renders. Mitigation: gate the form behind `if (loading || user) return null;` so it never mounts for authed users.
